data.name: The Basement Collection
data.detailed_description:
The Basement Collection is a compilation of 9 award winning indie games by Edmund McMillen, creator of Super Meat Boy and The Binding of Isaac. All of the games featured in the collection have been revamped and updated, featuring bonus chapters, new music, art and other extras.
The Basement Collection includes:
  • Aether ( an exploration adventure game )
  • Time Fcuk ( a dark puzzle game )
  • Spewer ( a physics based platformer )
  • Meat Boy ( the super meat boy prototype )
  • Grey Matter ( an anti shooter )
  • Coil (an experimental game )
  • Triachnid (a physics based spider sim)
The collection also features 2 secret unlockable games and tons of unlockable comics, sketch books and even never before scene stock footage from Indie Game: The Movie.

Key Features

  • 8 full games, featuring new content, achievements and development extras.
  • 8 unlockable extras featuring bonus games, comics, sketch books and videos.
  • A full collection soundtrack, featuring over 30 full length tracks from games featured as well as fan made bonus tracks.
  • Over 30 minutes of audio interviews.
  • Over 20 minutes of video extras from Indie Game: The Movie, (15 minutes of never before scene footage).
  • Over 15 pages of development sketches and character designs.

reviews.review:
i got took by a random urge to play the basement collection again and i dunno why. it might be because some of my friends are obsessed with mewgenics, so i kept being reminded of edmund's earlier games that i enjoyed.
if you've enjoyed flash games or the collections that are on steam, this is a must buy without question

the first surprise was that this compilation is (almost) 15 fcuking years old!!
flash game compilations have been popping up ever since flash stopped being supported in 2020 and they've been my go-to casual stuff, and the basement collection might be the earliest forma of them. i think the next best one for me is jmtb02's elephant collection, which took some cues from here with its unlockable dev comments. but i think the basement collection has made me  hold the others to a way higher standard than they were aiming for, something i feel like i never realised that until now

the second is that i enjoyed revisiting the basement collection way more than i thought i would.
initially i was expecting to just bumble through it and get it out of my system, but pretty much every game (except for one (and the joke game riffing mobile game habits that's still relevant unfortunately)) gripped me in some way.
maybe a bit too much since i felt compelled to get the achievements here, but a lot of these games are better when you enjoy them at your own pace and leaving the bonus stuff only if you're really fiending for a bit extra out of a short freeware game- but a good 90% of my misery was entirely avoidable and self-inflicted.

what makes this collection for me is the bonus content that comes with it: the full Q&As, dev sketches and concept art, and bonus unlockable comics that might explain why some of edmund's games are like that. the flash stuff i've enjoyed the most has always very personal, they always have the creator's marks  all over them, and the pieces included really help
this is the most i've watched of indie game: the movie outside of the jonathan blow clip which might make me a fake 00's PC gamer, but the clips are a lot more engaging when you're fresh off of having played the game. sometimes the clip might reference something of edmund's: like an old comic he drew 
or a box of childhood drawings, then the unlock for 100%-ing the game discussed in the clip will be the full collection of comics or drawings. it makes these concept art unlocks so much more fascinating than when games used to drop them in with no context (though i am starting to lament concept art unlocks falling out of style) 

having the behind the scenes stuff being so front-up on the menu is way better for making me wanna look and listen, and it's instilled in me a serious want to see other games build in commentaries like this. with a lot of stuff getting updated rereleases, remasters and whole ass redos it's made me wish they all came with stuff so nicely put together as how the basement collection's done it.

thankfully the games are mostly bangers too - as long as you don't torture yourself for the achievements like i mentioned. i'd say the only real dud is grey matter, an avoid-the-projectiles shmup adjacent game where it controls so whack you're just as likely to run into the projectiles. apart from that they're all premo flash fun that range the whole spectrum of tones: you can go from the sombre and cutely nihilistic aether to artsy grief poem coil to funny goo puke spewer and finish it off with time fcuk which wrangles all of the tones together. after the binding of isaac and (assuming from what i've seen of) mewgenics being a lot of the spewer style puke and piss and poop untethered irreverence, it was pretty refreshing to go back and see the teams exploring a few different emotions here.

it helps that the games are pretty fun to actually play, sans a few classic edmund moments where a level in the required path sucks mondo ass.
meat boy has such a fun weight and control that you can see why it was spun into a full title, flash physics seen in spewer and triachnid will always make me clap like a buffoon and time fcuk's banger main theme made me wanna keep playing which lead to the extremely bad decision of doing the user-level gauntlet. aether's such a nice game all around, to where hearing edmund's plans for a super meat boy style follow up that still hasn't came to be is a real bummer.
even AVGM fits into the more emotional side of the collection: if only because it's a parody of mobile game skinnerbox tactics that have only gotten worse in the 15 years since and it bums me out

anyways i hope edmund uses the mewgenics money to make another time fcuk sequel
